summary_html: Findings by **federal/state oversight** (CFSR reviews, OIG audits, child-fatality commissions) can initiate investigations or corrective actions that open CPS involvement.
authority_html:
- **Protect Our Kids Act (PL 112-275)** — national commission on child abuse/neglect fatalities  
- **Child & Family Services Reviews (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal monitoring of state systems  
- **Inspector General Act (5 U.S.C. App.)** — OIG oversight of HHS/ACF and grantees

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held the 'reasonable efforts' clause of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act does not unambiguously confer an enforceable federal right on the Act's beneficiaries and Congress created no private remedy, leaving enforcement to the Secretary's funding mechanisms and state judicial findings.
key_cases.relevance: Federal oversight of state performance runs through administrative review and funding conditions rather than private suit.
key_cases.quote: we think that Congress did not intend to create a private remedy for enforcement of the “reasonable efforts” clause

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the order compelling release of the budget-reduction plans the Department of Family Services and the Department of Health had submitted to the Governor, holding the plans were factual rather than deliberative, and declined to decide whether the Wyoming Public Records Act incorporates a deliberative process privilege at all.
key_cases.relevance: Public disclosure of agency records is how outside oversight bodies obtain the material that triggers systemic review.
key_cases.quote: The plans contain factual information, rather than opinions, deliberations or thought processes and are not, therefore, the sort of documents protected by the deliberative process privilege.

key_cases.case_name: Circuit Court of the Eighth Judicial District v. Lee Newspapers
key_cases.holding: The Court held that court proceedings and judicial documents in child sexual-assault cases must generally remain open, with redaction and initials used to satisfy the victim-confidentiality statute, and that closure requires an on-the-record finding of a compelling interest, narrowly tailored, after a hearing open to the public.
key_cases.relevance: Public access to the court record is the mechanism by which outside observers detect systemic failures in child cases.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court must find that there is a compelling interest in closing the court proceedings and sealing the case file which is essential to preserve higher values

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-205(a)

Staff of a medical or other public or private institution, school, facility or agency must also notify the person in charge, who is then also responsible for making the report — Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-205(b)

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Notification of a suspected case of child abuse or neglect
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in statute; Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-204(a)(iii) states the duty without a penalty, and the agency must seek a court order if denied reasonable access to the child

parent_rights_at_moment: Right to refuse entry without warrant
Right to be advised of the specific complaints or allegations against you at the initial time of contact (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-204(a)(iii))
A DFS caseworker cannot take your child: only a law enforcement officer, a treating physician, physician's assistant or nurse practitioner, or a court order can (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-405)
what_to_say: I do not consent to entry without a warrant
Please provide your card and the allegations in writing
I will have my attorney contact you
what_not_to_do: Do not let them in 'just to look'
